item.title: Texas Longhorns are ranked 6th in the College Football Playoff. Here's what it means
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning celebrates after beating Mississippi at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football would qualify for the College Football Playoff if the regular season ended before this weekend's slate of games. But the Longhorns' spot in the college football's postseason tournament still isn't secure with three games remaining. On Tuesday, Texas was ranked the No. 6 team in the latest CFP rankings. Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) dodges Texas A&M Aggies safety Dalton Brooks (25) to run the ball in for a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the Lone Star Showdown, the rivalry match-up between the Longhorns and Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Nov. 28, 2025. The Longhorns won the game 17-27. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Steve Sarkisian 's team dropped two games in October to unranked opponents in Oklahoma and Florida . The defeats make Texas one of six two-loss teams in the current 12-team playoff field, a number that will likely grow in the coming weeks. Ten two-loss teams have qualified for the College Football Playoff across the last two years. Its rare to see a three-loss playoff team, however, with the only two exceptions (Clemson in 2024 and Alabama in 2025) being teams that played in their conference championship game. GOLDEN : Longhorns shows they can win a tough road game - and a whole lot more FILM STUDY : Arch Manning made this winning move vs. Mizzou Texas is safe for now. But will a third loss this season knock Sarkisian and Co. out of the the Playoff? >And what games should Texas fans be on the lookout for this week? Texas has simple route to CFP qualification Let's not complicate matters. Win each of the next three games, and Texas is effectively guaranteed CFP inclusion. The Longhorns' seeding would then be the biggest question, one with multiple potential answers. Texas could close the regular season with wins over LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M and still miss the SEC championship, then reach the CFP as a 10-2 at-large selection. Being an at-large team likely mean Texas would host a first-round game or hit the road for one. UT would, of course, qualify for the CFP if it did make and win the SEC championship, a scenario in which the Longhorns would then likely receive a top-four seed and subsequent first-round bye. Would Texas be in jeopardy of missing the playoff if it won the next three games, then lost the SEC championship? Unlikely. Alabama's CFP inclusion last year provides the proper precedent. Lose your third game in the conference title game, and you won't incur a penalty. For Texas, the formula remains simple: win the next three games, and the championship chase will stay alive, regardless of the conference result. item.title: Latest Tarik Skubal Report Puts Dodgers At Real Disadvantage In Sweepstakes
item.description: Free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal If not for an impending lockout, Tarik Skubal's free agency would have every headline in baseball this offseason. The two-time Cy Young Award winner is set up to sign a record-breaking contract in the coming weeks, and according to ESPN's Jeff Passan, Skubal wants to not only get paid, but he wants a lengthy deal. "Certainly the Dodgers will be in the mix on Skubal, but to what extent is unclear," wrote Passan on Wednesday. "Unlike Kyle Tucker last offseason, Skubal has no interest in a shorter-term, higher-dollar deal, which could disadvantage the Dodgers when contending with the New York Mets (or the San Diego Padres or Toronto Blue Jays)." The Dodgers have excelled at signing players to deals with deferred money or short deals with high total value. However, it's not like they cannot dish out longer contracts. They did so for Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, with everything going on with Mark Walter outside of baseball right now, it may be a little more difficult for them to dish out a double-digit-year deal. However, it's not impossible. At the end of the day, they are still the Dodgers and should be able to compete with anyone financially. However, they are coming off a sweep in the National League Championship Series in which their offense disappeared. They won back-to-back World Series with weaker rotations than the one they trotted out in October this year, and they need to evaluate if spending big on Skubal is really what they need. “He was awesome to get to know,’’ Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said on Tuesday, per USA Today's Bob Nightengale. “He fit in great into the clubhouse. Obviously, we know what kind of pitcher he is. So, for us, it’s understanding what this all looks like, as far as what does our team need? What does the contract look like? Where does he end up? I don’t know.’’ The Dodgers may not think it's the best idea to sign Skubal to a long-term deal, and if that's what he desires, the Dodgers will really have to hope the allure of winning can get him to change his mind. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Ciryl Gane Reveals How Jon Jones Defeat Changed His Mindset as a UFC Fighter
item.description: Jon Jones beats Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight title at UFC 285 | Photo: @ufcespanol/YouTube | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Ciryl Gane is preparing for his first heavyweight title defense against Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334. The Frenchman was recently elevated to undisputed champion after Tom Aspinall vacated the title due to further complications with his eye injury. However, much of the attention surrounding the Madison Square Garden headliner has focused on Gane’s legitimacy as champion and the growing criticism of his illegal tactics inside the Octagon. While the Frenchman has pushed back against accusations of being a dirty fighter, he recently made another revealing admission ahead of his showdown. Gane opened up about his defeat to Jon Jones at UFC 285 , describing the experience as a major turning point in his career. The reigning champion also reflected on how the loss affected his confidence and changed his mindset as a fighter. Ciryl Gane Explains How His UFC 285 Loss to Jon Jones Fueled His Comeback At UFC 285 in March 2023, Jones made his long-awaited heavyweight debut after nearly four years away from competition. He challenged Gane for the vacant heavyweight championship, with the Frenchman entering the contest fresh off a knockout victory over Tai Tuivasa at UFC Paris. Many expected Gane to provide Jones with a difficult test, considering the latter was moving up a division and returning after an extended layoff. However, the fight unfolded very differently. Despite taking an early groin strike, Jones quickly took control of the contest, secured a takedown and locked in a guillotine choke. Gane was forced to tap in less than three minutes, handing Jones his second UFC championship. Speaking in a recent interview with UFC on Paramount+ , Gane reflected on the defeat and said, “I think it was after the Jon Jones loss because it was a real loss.” Although Gane had already suffered his first professional MMA defeat against Francis Ngannou at UFC 270, that fight went the distance, with the Cameroonian winning by unanimous decision. The loss to Jones, however, was a much more decisive setback. Gane explained, “The fight against Francis Ngannou was a little bit square, but after Jon Jones, something changed in my mindset because also the pressure of social media from everywhere.” The 36-year-old further opened up about the criticism he received and the doubts he had about continuing his career. He added, “Like, ‘Ciryl Gane, we overestimated him,’ blah, blah, blah. I was disappointed. It was 2023, and I started MMA in 2019, so I already did pretty much in four years. One side of my head was about to give my back to everyone, but because I’m a competitor and because I want to prove to myself, I’m going to stay. I’m going to prove to myself.'” Since that setback, Gane has remained unbeaten, defeating Alexander Volkov at UFC 310 before earning another heavyweight title opportunity against Aspinall at UFC 321

item.title: Orlando pro wrestler Onix Caballero to make sumo debut against MMA champion
item.description: Orlando professional wrestler Onix “The One” Caballero is scheduled to make his sumo debut against Joe “The Party” Penafiel on Nov. 21 at Caribe Royale Orlando. Danielle Flores Orlando professional wrestler Onix “The One” Caballero will trade wrestling rules for sumo when he faces MMA fighter Joe “The Party” Penafiel on Nov. 21 at Caribe Royale Orlando. The open-weight matchup will be contested as a best-of-three-rounds “Sumo Superfight,” according to World Elite Sumo. Tickets are available online . Caballero, 31, was born and raised in Caguas, Puerto Rico, and lives in Orlando. Organizers identify him as the reigning Real Radio Monsters heavyweight wrestling champion. A former competitive football player, Caballero began professional wrestling five years ago and has competed in promotions including Major League Wrestling, according to the announcement. An Orlando matchup Penafiel, 36, also fights out of Orlando. The Ecuador-born fighter holds a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt and has held championships in three MMA promotions, organizers said. The bout will mark Caballero’s first competition under sumo rules. One-night tournament The event, “World Elite Sumo: Pro Era V,” will also feature a 12-man, open-weight tournament. Orlando’s Aaron “Coringa” Conway was announced as the final entrant. item.title: 'Need to find a replacement': Irfan Pathan identifies Punjab Kings' weak link after blockbuster Hardik-Arshdeep exchange
item.description: The blockbuster trade between Mumbai Indians (MI) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) has triggered plenty of discussion around the possible playing combinations of both franchises ahead of IPL 2027. While Punjab have strengthened their batting with the arrival of Indian all-rounder Hardik Pandya, they have also parted ways with one of their most dependable fast bowlers, Arshdeep Singh. Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has weighed in on the high-profile exchange, highlighting the benefits of Hardik's arrival for Punjab while raising concerns over their bowling resources following Arshdeep's departure. Taking to X, Pathan pointed out that Hardik's addition would provide Punjab with a much-needed power-hitting option in the middle and lower order. "With this trade of Hardik, Punjab get a really good middle and lower order power hitter. Their batting line-up was already strong, but this makes them even stronger in that department. "Their bowling is a real concern for me. They not only need to find a replacement for Arshdeep Singh but also need to invest in a good spinner going forward," Pathan wrote. — IrfanPathan (@IrfanPathan) Hardik Pandya joins Punjab Kings in blockbuster trade The trade sees Hardik return to a new franchise after his second stint with Mumbai Indians, while Arshdeep brings his seven-year association with Punjab Kings to an end. Hardik will join Punjab Kings for a fee of Rs 18 crore, up from his previous retention fee of Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep, meanwhile, will move to Mumbai Indians at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore. Hardik's arrival adds considerable experience and firepower to Punjab's batting unit. The all-rounder has featured in 162 IPL matches, scoring 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 while picking up 82 wickets. However, Arshdeep's departure leaves a significant gap in Punjab's bowling attack. The left-arm pacer was the franchise's leading wicket-taker, claiming 111 wickets in 96 IPL appearances. item.title: Kenyon Martin Defends LeBron James For Helping Bronny Reach The NBA Despite Not Being Ready
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Kenyon Martin believes Bronny James entered the NBA a year too soon. He still understands why LeBron James would use his influence to help his son get there. In Martin’s view, any parent in LeBron’s position would do the same, even if Bronny would have benefited from another season at USC. Speaking on the TFU podcast , Martin addressed the criticism that has followed Bronny since the Los Angeles Lakers selected him with the No. 55 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Martin said that he did not question the influence of James’ name, but he also questioned why parents would pass on the chance to influence their own child’s future. “With Bronny and LeBron, yes, nepotism is real. We all know it and we all would do it. If we had the opportunity to do it, 1000%. If any one of us are able to put our child in a position to succeed and have direct influence on it, we would. No doubt about it.” “Do I think Bronny at the time was ready for the NBA? No. Because of his lack of college experience that he had. It was interrupted because of the heart thing. Would loved to have seen him at USC another year to just get playing time. Get used to being back on the floor without all the pressures of what came with making that decision to being in the NBA, and your last name being James.” “And without all the pressures and scrutiny of everything that came with being the 55th pick in the NBA draft, which no other 55th pick has those kind of expectations. We get it. His last name is James, but it’s unfair to the kid. He’s still a kid. But it’s their family. It’s their decision and wish them nothing but the best.” Bronny suffered a cardiac arrest at a USC practice before the season even began. He returned to play 25 games, starting six, averaging 4.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. Martin did say that he would have wanted Bronny to spend another year at USC and get regular minutes to find his rhythm before dealing with the attention that came with joining his father in Los Angeles. The attention obviously cuts both ways. Being LeBron’s son gave Bronny a chance that most prospects won’t even have, but it has also meant that every shot can come under the microscope, whether in the NBA or not. Most No. 55 picks get to develop before being expected to contribute off the bench. Bronny never had that luxury. Now in his third season, the 22-year-old is yet to secure a regular rotation role in JJ Redick’s lineup. Through his first five NBA appearances this season, he’s averaged just 0.8 points. item.title: Malik Nabers Shuts Down Broadcast Critics With Raw Honesty
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Malik Nabers refused to let a TV crew define his character after Sunday’s win. The Giants wide receiver called the broadcast critique a “lie” and said he will keep speaking his mind. Calling Out the Narrative Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen spent time talking about Nabers during the game. They pointed to his reaction on the sideline and claimed his body language was poor. Nabers saw this on social media and decided to strike back. “I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying,” Nabers said in comments reported by the New York Post . He said he will not change his behavior to please strangers watching from home. The criticism came after a tough first half where the Giants struggled to score. Nabers spiked his helmet when his team only managed field goals. His streak of four straight 100-yard games ended in that contest, leaving him with 43 yards on five catches. “One thing about it is that I’m an ultimate competitor whether it’s going [well] or if it’s going bad,” Nabers told reporters per the New York Post. He said his intense style comes from a deep passion for the sport, not anger, and he expects others to share that passion. A Direct Challenge to Olsen The former NFL tight end Greg Olsen suggested Nabers was unhappy for teammate Isaiah Likely after a touchdown. Olsen implied Nabers was not a good teammate because of how he carried himself on the field. Nabers rejected this idea entirely and said he has never been called a bad teammate before. “I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate,” Nabers stated according to ESPN . He noted that he holds everyone to a high standard of playing “mean” and getting the team fired up. Nabers said he would welcome a simple conversation with Olsen if the analyst wants to talk. He wants to clear the air but will not apologize for his competitiveness. “If he wants to reach out, he can reach out. We can have a civil conversation,” Nabers said per the New York Post. The Giants star emphasized that no one else can speak for him, so he must use his own voice to set the record straight. Focus Shifts to Washington The Giants (5-2-1) hold first place in their division after beating the Eagles 19-11. Nabers said he is already moving past the broadcast drama to focus on the next opponent. He mentioned that the long year of rehab he endured to return from a torn ACL, fuels his drive this season. The team now prepares for a Thursday night game against the Washington Commanders. That matchup is set for Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

item.description: Harry Kane will set a new England record of 126 appearances when he features in a Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley (John Walton) England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career. When Kane leads England out at Wembley to earn his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton since 1990. It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals, as well as holding Tottenham Hotspur's all-time mark with 280. Since leaving Spurs to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level. He has amassed 156 goals for the German club, finally winning the first silverware of his career with Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026. But breaking Shilton's long-standing record also matters to Kane, who told a pre-match press conference on Wednesday: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement). "I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career." For all Kane's brilliance, England have not won a major men's international trophy since lifting the 1966 World Cup on home soil. And Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as England were beaten by Argentina in the semi-finals of the World Cup. - 'Beautiful occasion' - England were leading 1-0 until late in the game but could not score again, with manager Thomas Tuchel criticised for packing the team's defence only for Argentina to score twice late on as Kane was denied a first appearance in a World Cup final. "In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits -- 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," added Kane. "We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages. I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve." Tuchel, speaking earlier Wednesday, was coy when asked if Kane was England's greatest footballer. "I don't know. He's up there of course. It's now proven. It's always nice if things are proven in sports -- he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games. "Tomorrow he will start for us and as captain. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion." item.description: Earning the top seed is one thing. Living up to the expectations that come with it is another. And on Tuesday, St. Mary's volleyball offered another reminder of why its program has claimed five Northern California championships, 14 Sac-Joaquin Section titles and 32 league championships. One week after a CIF Sac-Joaquin Section semifinal loss , top-seeded St. Mary's bounced back with a dramatic CIF State Division II first-round victory over No. 16 Cardinal Newman, the North Bay-Oak League's first-place finisher, at Anthony Morelli Gym, 19-25, 25-16, 25-17, 22-25, 15-13. "We weren't at our best," St. Mary's coach Garren Allala said. "But sometimes you have to find a way to hold on, stick with it and be resilient. You can't blink. Sometimes it's OK to win ugly, and I'm glad we got it out of the way now." For a St. Mary's team that finished the regular season with 80 consecutive Tri-City Athletic League victories, the fifth set brought a different kind of challenge. The Rams trailed 11-9 and later 13-12 before pulling out the win. "I was a little stressed for a while there," senior outside hitter Shea Hardcastle said. "I couldn't breathe for a second. I'm just so happy for us. We pulled through. God's got us." Through it all, junior libero and UC Santa Barbara commit Rachel Nemee was doing what Allala has come to call her "the backbone" for. Willing to put her body on the line and do the dirty work, Nemee finished with a career-high 38 digs. That brought her career total to 1,126, setting a St. Mary's school record. "I didn't even know until the very end," Nemee said. "I just broke down in tears. I'm so happy. I'm going to put that record so far out of reach. I want to keep it forever, like to the grave. This program has been so special to me, and it wouldn't be possible without the girls beside me." And those girls had plenty to do with it. item.title: NFL Panic Meter: While other NFC contenders loaded up at deadline, Rams and Lions were quiet
item.description: The theme of the trade deadline seemed to be contenders being more aggressive than ever before in their pursuit of a Super Bowl, particularly in the NFC. That's what made the inactivity of the Detroit Lions and Los Angeles Rams a bit startling. The Seattle Seahawks, Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers all made trades to help themselves now. The Green Bay Packers did not, but they're getting Micah Parsons back soon and they're relying on that being a big midseason addition. The 49ers did the least of that group, but they're also having the best season in the conference and starting to get a little healthier. And we don't need to count anyone in the NFC East or NFC South as a contender. The only move the Rams or Lions made was Detroit trading a sixth-round pick to the Jets for safety Andre Cisco, who was a part-time starter for a bad New York team. Let's start with the Rams, because they had the biggest need and their inactivity goes against their normal mode. The Rams have lost Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to injuries, and don't know if they'll be back before it's too late. They're dreadfully thin at receiver for the next few weeks, at least. The Rams have gone from preseason Super Bowl favorite to probably a slight underdog to even make the playoffs. Yet, they did not make a trade before the deadline. The Rams could argue, like the Packers, that adding Myles Garrett back is their in-season addition. But that doesn't help at receiver, and it's hard to believe the Rams have championship upside building a passing game around three or four tight ends and nothing else. It seems like the Rams put three-quarters of their chips in the middle, then folded. The Lions probably could have used a cornerback or linebacker nearly as much as the Rams needed a receiver, but they did nothing other than a low-cost move to add Cisco. Detroit's defense probably isn't good enough to win a championship, and their fans will be frustrated after seeing other teams, particularly in the NFC North, make moves. They were clamoring for a cornerback for weeks and Jack Campbell's injury left them with a weakness at linebacker. Those areas of need still exist. The Rams have a "forget them picks" attitude but it still has a limit. They gave up a lot to get Garrett and Trent McDuffie in the offseason. They might have also privately seen a team that is slipping further from being a Super Bowl contender and didn't want to chase their losses. The Lions didn't want to pay the escalating prices to make a huge move on the back end of their defense, and while that might be prudent for the long haul, Detroit fans don't want to be patient anymore. Maybe the Lions or Rams still make a deep playoff run, but they'll have to do it against teams that got much better over the past couple weeks. item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect While the New York Giants were reportedly one of the most aggressive teams in the J onathan Taylor trade market, a new report makes it seem like a deal was never really close to happening. The Giants are in a very different position than they were this time last year. On this week in 2025, they fired head coach Brian Daboll after a 2-8 start and were a team already looking ahead to the following year’s NFL Draft. However, their situation is far different in 2026. Heading into their Thursday night matchup against the Washington Commanders on the Week 10 NFL schedule , they own a 5-2-1 record and sit atop the NFC East. They seem to be getting better each week and had reason to be aggressive to improve the roster before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Heading into yesterday, the name most linked to the Giants was the Indianapolis Colts star. Yet, while they allegedly made an offer of a second- and fifth-round pick, the Colts did not accept, and Taylor will remain in Indiana for the rest of this season. The assumption is that the Colts were likely looking for a first-round pick in a trade for the three-time Pro Bowler. A new report from ESPN backs that up and confirms the Giants would have had to make an offer Indianapolis simply could not refuse to pry away a player they didn’t want to move. New York Giants never came close to meeting Indianapolis Colts trade price for Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis in Week 6. According to Dan Graziano, the “buzz” about a Taylor trade was far bigger than the Colts’ interest in moving him. While they moved several players before yesterday’s deadline, they were all on expiring contracts. The running back still has a couple of years left on his contract.
